goal: Implement 'Seeded Levels, Rerolls and Classic Gold' in PopBlocks: every Story level is generated per player from a salted seed behind a bot-win and difficulty-band gate; a stuck player can reroll their current level for gold (price falls 10% of first-clear gold per failure, free at 10); Classic mode earns gold per block popped and accepts an optional starting seed that never touches the Story.

metadata.project: PopBlocks - .NET 10 MAUI (Android) app plus pure-C# PopBlocks.Engine and xUnit tests

source_documents.spec: https://claude.ai/artifact/3zojaVEhGF1huC9Mes3oND (PopBlocks: Seeded Levels, Rerolls and Classic Gold (Spec))
source_documents.design_docs: docs/01-game-design.md, docs/02-architecture.md, docs/04-story-mode.md, docs/07-testing.md, docs/09-extending.md, docs/10-campaign-and-content.md, docs/story/economy.md
source_documents.precedence: The spec wins. Where the spec names a line number or default, verify it against the code before relying on it.

tool_notes.shell: git, dotnet, powershell (no Python on this machine). dotnet publish for Android, Check-Permissions.ps1 and the on-device timing must run on the Windows machine with Visual Studio 2026.
tool_notes.code_search / code_edit: read and change files under E:\PopBlocks
tool_notes.run_tests: dotnet test tests/PopBlocks.Tests. The Engine targets plain net10.0, so no emulator is needed.
tool_notes.manual_review: human gate: on-device playtest (Samsung S24 plus a low-end Android phone for timing) or product-owner decision

execution_notes: Order is the spec's: measure (M0), seed plumbing (M1), saves and identity (M2), gate and roll (M3), player-facing reroll (M4), prefetch (M5), Classic gold (M6), docs and balance (M7).

M6 engine steps (28, 29) need only the new save keys (step_10) and Mix32 (step_07), so Classic gold can ship first as its own release. The M6 UI wiring (step_30) is serialised after the GameViewModel work (step_21) only to avoid edit conflicts; move it earlier if M6 ships first.
Step ids are not strict execution order: dependencies are. step_05 and step_06 (M0 sweep and timing) run after step_08 (seed plumbing) because the sweep builds candidates with Get(level, seed).
Steps serialise on purpose where they edit the same file: LevelCatalog.cs (steps 08, 15, 25), GameViewModel.cs (steps 08, 12, 21, 25, 26, 30) and SaveKeys.cs/SaveCode.cs (step 10).
Each run_tests gate must pass before the next milestone starts. Cut an internal build after M4 and after M6.
Steps whose arguments.optional is true can be skipped without affecting the rest of the plan.
Every number named in the spec is a starting value: keep it in one config class (step_07) and tune it from the sweep and playtests rather than hard-coding it.
Line numbers quoted from the spec (GameEngine.cs:187, GameViewModel.cs:778 and :836) were correct when the spec was written. Re-find the call sites by name before editing.
global_constraints: Legacy seed 0 must give byte-identical levels. LevelSnapshotTests (levels 1-220) must pass untouched and must not be regenerated. LevelCatalog.Get(n) keeps returning the legacy level so the ~100 existing call sites keep working.
The ten tutorial lessons stay hand-made and frozen. Level 11 keeps its scripted opening piece and intro card.

The seed may change the board and pieces but never a level's structure: goal kinds, goal count, intro goal, flip, no-pop penalty, finale, ability lock, exotic share, fall speed, colours and goal sizes keep coming from the level number and tier tables (PickKinds keeps Random(n * 7919 + 13)).
A level shown to a player is always bot-verified. Never use the unverified fallback level (Pop 8 blocks, 40 moves) for a rolled seed.
Offline only: no INTERNET permission, no analytics, no network packages, no new PackageReference unless unavoidable.
Rules live in PopBlocks.Engine. The MAUI app only draws and wires input.
SaveKeys are frozen: add keys, never rename or reuse. save_version stays 1; absent keys load as defaults, so no migration step.
Gold is earned and spent through the same path the shop uses so the 0 to 100,000,000 clamp and save-on-change apply. Integer arithmetic only.
Gold must never gate the story: the reroll is free at 10 failures, and the hint button is never the only way forward.

No countdowns, timers, pulsing or urgent colours on the reroll button. Every new control has an accessibility label that includes the price or state. Prices and states are plain text, never colour alone.
The loading card has no control that delays play and never shows a scene the player has not seen.
Classic never reads the player salt, the first-clear list or the failure counter.
A seeded Classic run pays gold at the normal rate but never updates best_score.
If an engine rule changes, change LevelSolver too and keep the catalogue replay test green. Add a seeded variant of the replay test instead of editing the old one.
Never hold the level-cache lock while the solver runs. Builds are single-flight per key. Run the Roll search off the UI thread.
Docs, the About page and the store listing change in the same commit as any promise they describe.

decisions_resolved.identical_levels: Dropped. Levels are generated per player.
decisions_resolved.player_salt: In-game name plus 32 random install bits, hashed once with FNV-1a, stored as player_salt, never recomputed
decisions_resolved.story_seed: Mix32(salt, level, reroll, attempt) & 0x3FFFFFFF, never 0. Goal kinds still come from the level number only.
decisions_resolved.legacy_seed: Seed 0 = today's n-based seeds, no difficulty gate. Used for levels cleared before the update, all existing tests and the frozen snapshot.
decisions_resolved.reroll_availability: After the first failure on the current level (HighestCleared + 1). Free at any time on replays of cleared levels.
decisions_resolved.reroll_price: (reward * (10 - min(failures, 10)) + 9) / 10 with reward = GoldRewards.For(level, false). Free at 10 failures. Levels 1-10 pay no gold so are always free.
decisions_resolved.failure: A loss, or a manual restart after at least one piece was placed. Leaving to the menu does not count. Losing on purpose is allowed.
decisions_resolved.failure_counter: Saved on every increment. Not reset by a reroll. Reset when the level is cleared.
decisions_resolved.cleared_levels: First-clear seed recorded once in the same place gold is paid, shown on the levels page, never overwritten. Every later seed is discarded.
decisions_resolved.difficulty: Hard requirements plus a hardness band (20th-80th percentile of min(2.0, weakNeed/fullNeed), smoothed over 5 levels each side inside a tier), softer at tier starts and mechanic introductions.
decisions_resolved.search: attempt 0-23 or 2 seconds, then the verified candidate closest to the band. Never an unverified level.
decisions_resolved.loading: Prefetch so rerolls are instant; otherwise a skippable recap card after 300 ms, held at least 600 ms.
decisions_resolved.classic_gold: rate(L) = min(5, 1 + (L - 1) / 4) tenths of a gold per block popped, carry saved as classic_gold_carry, banked once at game over / leave / background.
decisions_resolved.classic_seed: Optional 0 to 2,147,483,647. Piece i from new Random(Mix32(seed, i)). Seeded runs pay gold but never set best_score.

open_questions.question: Which levels can be rerolled?
open_questions.default: Every Story level including finales and level 200. The free reroll at 10 failures keeps gold from gating the story.

open_questions.question: Does a seeded Classic run count for the personal best?
Does a manual restart count as a failure?
open_questions.default: Yes, after at least one piece was placed. Leaving to the menu does not count.

open_questions.question: Skipped name?
open_questions.default: "Traveller". Optional extra: Pip uses the name in dialogue.

open_questions.question: Retuning after release: stored seeds are not regenerated, so a broken level cannot be fixed by retuning alone.
open_questions.default: Accept this for the first release. Later option: store generator_version and silently reroll uncleared levels made by an older version (a separate follow-up, not part of this plan).

open_questions.question: Classic HUD counter?
open_questions.default: Include the small running +N gold. Remove it if it distracts.

tunable_parameters.default: 20th to 80th percentile of hardness, smoothed over 5 levels each side
First 5 levels of a tier (51, 101, 151); each introduction level plus 2. Read introduction levels from the RegionRules constants.
Show after 300 ms, hold at least 600 ms
1 to 5 tenths of a gold per block by Classic level; a decent early run pays about 15 gold

Device timing: run the generation of a spread of levels on a low-end Android phone and record the 95th percentile per tier. If p95 is above 1 second, lower the attempt count (24) or skip the weak-bot run where it is not needed.
Choose and record: band percentiles (default 20th-80th), smoothing window (5), soft-start clamp rules, attempt count and time budget.

Callable off the UI thread; no shared mutable state without the single-flight cache.

steps.description: Engine rules for reroll: PricingRules (price function), FailureTracker (counted only on the current level, saved on every increment), and an atomic RerollService.

arguments.name: reroll_rules
details: price = (reward * (10 - min(failures, 10)) + 9) / 10, reward = GoldRewards.For(level, false). Offered when failures >= 1 on the current level (HighestCleared + 1); always free on a cleared level; levels 1-10 are always free.
Failure = loss, or manual restart after at least one piece placed. Leaving to the menu does not count. Replays never count.
Reroll in one save: deduct gold, reroll count + 1, clear the stored seed. Do this before generating. Too little gold changes nothing.
Spend gold through the shop's path so the clamp and save-on-change behaviour apply.
Examples to assert: level 12 -> 12/11/6/2/0; level 60 -> 33/30/17/4/0; level 130 -> 77/70/39/8/0; level 180 -> 114/103/57/12/0 at first-clear / 1 / 5 / 9 / 10+ failures.
acceptance: Table-driven pricing test including rounding
Free for levels 1-10 and at 10 or more failures
Spending is atomic; too little gold changes nothing
Failures survive an app restart, are not reset by a reroll, are reset by a clear

steps.description: First-clear record and seed resolution: write n:seed once in PlayerProgress.Complete, reset the current-level state, and implement the 'which seed a level plays' table.

arguments.name: first_clear_and_resolution
details: On the first clear of level n, in the same place gold is paid, write n:seed to first_clear_seeds. Never overwrite. Then reset stored seed 0, rerolls 0, failures 0.

Resolver: current level first entry -> Roll(level, salt, 0) stored; later entries -> stored seed; cleared level with record -> recorded seed; cleared before the update with no record -> legacy seed 0; reroll on a cleared level -> Roll(level, salt, k) with k per session, free, not stored; locked level -> not playable.
Leaving a rerolled replay returns the level to its recorded seed next time.
Memory objectives belong to the memory id, not the seed. Confirm against BonusObjectiveTests.
acceptance: Seed recorded once and never overwritten
A level cleared before the update replays the legacy seed
A reroll on a cleared level is not stored
Earning a memory objective on any seed counts

steps.description: Classic gold engine: rate table, run accrual in tenths, carry, and exactly-once banking. Independent of the Story work; needs only the new save keys.

arguments.name: classic_gold_engine
files: src/PopBlocks.Engine/Logic/ScoringSystem.cs or GameEngine.cs (expose blocks popped per wave)
details: rate(L) = min(5, 1 + (L - 1) / 4) tenths per block, using the Classic level (1 + score / 800) at the moment of the pop. Count every block in every wave, chain waves included, no chain multiplier, no drop points.
Pending tenths accrue during a run. Bank: total = carry + pending; gold += total / 10; carry = total % 10; pending = 0. Save classic_gold_carry.
Bank through the shop's gold path. Guard so each banking event pays exactly once (game over then leave pays once).
Integer arithmetic only.
acceptance: Rate table test for levels 1-4, 5-8, 9-12, 13-16, 17+
Carry is preserved across runs and stays in 0..9
Game over followed by leave pays once
Story levels pay no Classic gold

steps.description: Classic seeded piece stream: piece i comes from new Random(Mix32(seed, i)); a seeded run pays gold but never updates best_score; Classic reads no Story state.

arguments.name: classic_seed_engine
details: Stream is independent of how the player played and works with undo and rewind. Identical colour counts give identical pieces; the early 4-to-5 colour step is the only difference.
Unseeded Classic behaves as today.
Seeded run: Submit(best_score) is skipped.
No dependency on player salt, first_clear_seeds or the failure counter.
acceptance: Same seed gives identical pieces across runs
Seeded run leaves best_score alone
Classic code path reads no Story state (test with a settings fake that throws on Story keys)

steps.description: Classic app wiring: bank on game over, on leaving Classic (Back, menu, new game) and on app background (the same hook as auto-pause); optional Seed field on the start screen; HUD running total; game-over '+N gold' and seed with copy button.

arguments.name: classic_ui_wiring
details: Seed field: numeric 0 to 2,147,483,647, collapsed behind a small 'Seed' link with a Clear button. Empty means a random seed chosen when the run starts.
Game over shows '+N gold' and the seed used (typed or random) with a copy button.
HUD: small running '+N gold', display only (Q6 default: include). Payment still happens only at the three banking events.
Save immediately after banking, as the personal best does today. A process killed with no event loses the unbanked part; that is accepted.

Backgrounding mid-run banks and saves
Seed field validation rejects out-of-range input
